_comment: MEASURED 2026-09-25 on a box with a google.com login, through `act` (browser 1.11.0), and NOTHING ELSE is relied on here. A compose URL with to= and su= opens full-screen compose with both fields filled, and Gmail DROPS a body= parameter (the first draft had an empty body), so the body is typed. The body fills at div[role=textbox][aria-label="Message Body"]. The Send button is a div[role=button] whose aria-label STARTS with Send (live: 'Send (Ctrl-Enter) Send', with bidi marks around the shortcut); clicking it is a `send` (exit 73) until the owner says yes, and after the yes the 'Message sent' toast appears. The Sent folder at #sent then lists the mail as a row under [role=main] carrying its subject. THE PROBE, measured on BOTH halves: logged out (2026-09-16, the plugin's probe with a throwaway profile) the sign-in page is 857 KB and its title is exactly 'Sign in - Google Accounts', 1 match; logged in (2026-09-26) `status google.com` read authenticated with this probe, 0 matches. It probes the sign-in page and not myaccount.google.com because a logged-out myaccount renders a marketing page with 0 matches, and its marker is the page's title, not the words 'Sign in'. The marker is a regex (grep -iE here, RegExp in the served browser); this one has no metacharacters.

send._comment: `guard: true`: the executor stops in front of the Send click (exit 73) exactly as `act` does, because the caller's arguments choose who gets the mail and what it says. The owner's yes (sudo 5dive browser approve <id>) is bound to this action with these exact --to/--subject/--body, once; re-run with --approved-id=<id>. The last step holds the tab until Gmail says the mail went: closing the browser the instant Send is clicked can cut the send off. It is a hold, not the verdict. If it never appears the step fails, and the re-read of Sent still decides.

verify._comment: The Sent folder is not a public page: a plain fetch of it is the sign-in page, so `in_session` re-reads it in this profile. `scope` grades only the FIRST row under [role=main], the newest mail, so an older mail with the same subject further down cannot pass for this one. That the first such row is the newest mail is Gmail's newest-first order, not a row-by-row measurement; the owner's live send is what confirms it. A first match that is not the new mail reads NOT VERIFIED, never verified.
